notes: Heavy copy edit, no rewrites. All dialogue lacked quotation marks (confusing for young readers) and now has them. Every mirror, spin, tiling and pentagon demo was replayed in chapters 3-5 as if it were new; those replays are cut or reframed (ch4 now checks the drawing against a knotted string measured from the gap over the gate). Maths fixes: six triangles make a hexagon, not a star; shapes are stated to have equal sides, since some five-sided shapes do tile; the gap-filling stars have five points, not eight; Sanjar gives the corner reason (three pentagon corners leave a gap, four overlap). notes: Science fixes: (1) Faraji's 'lowest and loudest' idea was backwards: a satellite low on the horizon is at its farthest and faintest. Now Aunt suggests the start of the pass and Faraji's Mama-at-the-door idea is 'closest = loudest', so they send in the middle, overhead. (2) A milk-carton satellite cannot be seen with the eye: in ch1 the moving star is the space station (still teaches the 90-minute orbit), and in ch3-4 they find Kijana by ear. This also removes ch3 re-teaching the 90-minute orbit as if it were new. Pass count: ch2 used up a stone with no pass. Now there are three passes and two stones, which is consistent. Faraji no longer climbs the rooftop water tank (unsafe to copy). Ch2 title nearly duplicated ch1. Malindi IS their town, so the photo line is fixed. Pass times now shift a little each night.

notes: The single chapter was titled 'First Pass' though it covers every pass; retitled. Fact fixes: orbital speed at 410 km is about 7.7 km/s, not 11; astronauts talk to hams on two metres, not 'two zero' (20 m, which a solar storm would black out); a 410 km orbit takes about 92 minutes; plasma does not appear the moment the burn ends (it comes about half an hour later), which also now fits the hour-plus to splashdown. Pass times now agree with Jory's 'four minutes later' fix: 03:10/04:42/06:14 become 03:14/04:46/06:18 (the old text heard the last pass earlier than the uncorrected time). Removed the Yaesu brand, and the radio now runs off a car battery as it does later in the chapter. Chosen not to fix: a burn over Cornwall would really bring the capsule down far along its track, not near a Newlyn trawler. That is in the brief and is the ending.
